evals.name: macos-update-blocked-by-space
evals.prompt: My 256GB Mac cannot install a macOS update. I use Expo, Swift, and Docker. Find the best cleanup candidates first.
evals.expected_output: Runs read-only discovery, follows large parents into identified subdirectories, proposes measured targets with consequences and exact cleanup methods, and obtains approval before deletion.
assertions: Reports the Data-volume/container baseline and any failed probes.
Does not sum overlapping parent/child sizes or promise a minimum recovery.
Does not delete anything during discovery.

evals.name: vague-disk-full-symptom
evals.prompt: My Mac is basically full again. What is taking up the space?
evals.expected_output: Uses the scanner and targeted follow-up reads, distinguishes candidate storage from approved cleanup, and surfaces unknown measurements.
assertions: Inspects hidden tool storage and large application folders.
Reports permission/service failures as unknown rather than empty.
Preserves application data while investigating its largest subdirectories.

evals.name: approved-safe-batch
evals.prompt: You already measured and proposed npm cache and one named DerivedData folder. I approve both; clean them now. The scan also lists Trash and a live iPhone simulator. You have since relabeled one approved item as APP-MANAGED, with no change to the target or consequences.
evals.expected_output: Rechecks the approved targets and active builds, cleans that batch, and verifies the result without asking again for the same approval.
assertions: Acts on the two approved targets without redundant confirmation.
Does not remove Trash or simulator state.
Uses an immediate before/after baseline.
Uses scoped target checks instead of requiring another full disk scan.
Does not treat a classification-label change as a new approval boundary.

evals.name: nested-conductor-build-cache
evals.prompt: RepoPrompt CE Application Support uses 17 GiB. The next level shows Conductor/BuildCache at 10 GiB and Codex/Release sessions and databases at 5 GiB. The repo has a conductor executable. What can we remove?
evals.expected_output: Reads developer-storage guidance, verifies current conductor cache commands and keys, and proposes only verified build-cache entries for cleanup.
assertions: Does not classify the entire Application Support directory as disposable.
Discovers keys from current status, not an example or previous run.
Preserves Codex session databases and task history.
Uses the native key-locking cache drop command after approval.

evals.name: docker-context-and-retained-version
evals.prompt: I use Docker Desktop. The active context is colima, whose image inventory returns I/O errors. Desktop is now running: postgres:16 and postgres:18 have zero container references; mysql:8 is referenced by a stopped container. Remove only postgres:16, since I still use v18.
evals.expected_output: Targets desktop-linux explicitly, verifies the selected image and references, removes only postgres:16, and checks retained images and host disk space.
assertions: Does not diagnose Docker Desktop from Colima errors.
Does not reset Colima or delete a raw VM disk.
Does not run broad image/system/volume prune.
Preserves v18, the MySQL container, and all data volumes.

evals.name: apfs-and-sparse-accounting
evals.prompt: du shows 11 GiB in a project .build and 10 GiB in an external cloned build cache. Docker.raw has a 60 GB logical size but du reports 2.8 GiB. How much can you guarantee we will recover?
evals.expected_output: Explains allocated, logical, shared, and reclaimable storage; proposes measurement after approved cleanup without guaranteeing the sum.
assertions: Does not promise 21 GiB from the two build paths.
Does not advertise 60 GB of Docker reclaimable space.
Does not infer snapshots or corruption from a recovery mismatch alone.

evals.name: simulator-runtime-retained-asset
evals.prompt: I approved removing my only simulator and its iOS runtime. simctl now lists zero devices and runtimes, but the MobileAsset backing download remains and free space rose only 3 GiB versus an 8 GiB image estimate.
evals.expected_output: Separately verifies device/runtime removal and retained host files, reports partial storage recovery, and leaves protected asset cleanup unresolved unless an authorized supported method is found.
assertions: Does not claim the whole 8 GiB was recovered.
Does not propose raw removal under /System/Library/AssetsV2.
Does not claim delete unavailable uninstalls shared runtimes.

evals.name: android-physical-device-only
evals.prompt: I use a physical Android phone. AVD and system-images folders are empty, but sdk/emulator is 965 MiB. Remove the emulator; keep local builds and debugging working. Command-line SDK management is absent.
evals.expected_output: Selects only the emulator program, tries an available native cleanup route, and uses a verified scoped fallback if package management is unusable.
assertions: Retains adb/platform-tools, build-tools, platforms, and project-required native tooling.
Does not download a fresh SDK or accept default setup packages just to uninstall.
Verifies the emulator package is gone and the retained tools still exist.

evals.name: claude-failed-telemetry
evals.prompt: Clean Claude failed telemetry files. The telemetry directory contains 1p_failed_events.*.json files with one event_type/event_data object per line, plus an unfamiliar notes file and a symlink. Claude projects and settings are elsewhere.
evals.expected_output: Checks only necessary file structure, treats the known files as JSON Lines, and deletes only approved matching regular files.
assertions: Preserves the notes file and symlink.
Does not print event payloads or erase projects/settings.
Reports remaining files and observed disk recovery.

evals.name: scanner-failed-probes-and-overlap
evals.prompt: The scanner cannot access DiskManagement or Time Machine. It measures Library/Caches at 5 GiB, including 3 GiB of browser cache and 1 GiB of Homebrew cache; the total simulator device folder is 5 GiB but no unavailable device inventory is available.
evals.expected_output: Reports unknown snapshot/container state and treats parent directories as investigation totals rather than additional cleanup candidates.
assertions: Does not report zero snapshots from a failed command.
Does not total 9 GiB from the cache parent and its children.
Does not classify all 5 GiB of device state as safe or reclaimable by delete unavailable.
